- "Imalat" vs "İmalat" — dotted İ vs plain I (accent/diacritic difference, Turkish)
- "Sirketi" vs "Şirketi" — Ş vs S (accent difference)

These are all spelling/accent/case differences of the same Turkish company name. Per the rules, accent differences and case differences = same-entity.

Best value: Since it's same-entity, the fused record should carry... The rule says "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity" but doesn't explicitly say which value. Typically the document is the legal instrument, so the document's form with correct Turkish characters would be preferred. Actually, in the extraction context, the register value appears to be a normalized ASCII version. The best value for a fused record — I'd pick the document's value since the certificate is the legal instrument and has proper Turkish orthography (İ, Ş). The rules specify best_value only for different-entity (document) and document-noise (register). For same-entity, either could work, but the document's canonical legal form makes sense. However, some fusion systems prefer the register's canonical form for consistency. The rules mention "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form" — that suggests for identifier-like axes, register canonical. For names, the document is the legal instrument.

I'll go with the document's value: "Esit Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi" — correct diacritics, from the legal instrument.
